Subject: The Agent Brief - Issue #38: agents that read your inbox

This week in AI agents

1) Inbox agents go mainstream
Several productivity startups shipped assistants that can triage email, draft replies, and book meetings on your behalf. Reviewers liked the time savings but flagged a familiar risk: when an agent reads untrusted text, that text can try to steer it. Security researchers call this indirect prompt injection.

2) What the defenses look like
Most teams are converging on the same few ideas: keep the model's instructions separate from content it reads, require a human to approve anything that sends data out, and log every tool call. None of these are silver bullets, but together they shrink the blast radius.

3) Benchmark watch
A new open benchmark measures how often agents follow instructions hidden in documents. Scores are improving, but no model is at zero yet.

Quote of the week: "Treat every email like it was written by a stranger - because it was."
